sec: Liver embryological derivatives and lobule structure

items.q: Match each embryological source with what it forms — 1) Endoderm 2) Mesoderm via septum transversum 3) Resident yolk sac macrophages 4) Vitelline vein greater than umbilical vein … A) Sinusoids B) Kupffer cells C) Hepatocytes and cholangiocytes D) Connective tissue, Glisson's capsule and stellate or Ito cells
items.exp: The derivatives table pairs endoderm with hepatocytes and cholangiocytes, mesoderm through the septum transversum with connective tissue, Glisson's capsule and stellate cells, resident yolk sac macrophages with Kupffer cells, and the vitelline to umbilical vein channel with the sinusoids. (Book p983)

items.q: All of the following are listed as products of the septum transversum mesoderm EXCEPT:
items.exp: The mesoderm row of the table covers connective tissue, Glisson's capsule and the stellate cells, whereas Kupffer cells occupy their own row as resident yolk sac macrophages. (Book p983)

items.q: Under the heading Anatomy the page opens with which unit, described as the structural and functional unit?
items.exp: The only unit named on this page is the lobule, bullet-pointed as the structural and functional unit before its structure is diagrammed. (Book p983)

items.q: The blood supply and oxygen supply figures printed beside the diagram read which pair for portal vein and hepatic artery?
opts: 70% and 30% of blood flow, 40% and 60% of oxygen
60% and 40% of blood flow, 70% and 30% of oxygen
50% and 50% of blood flow, 40% and 60% of oxygen
70% and 30% of blood flow, 30% and 70% of oxygen
items.exp: The diagram annotates the portal vein as 70 over 40 and the hepatic artery as 30 over 60, under the two column headings blood supply and oxygen supply, so the vein carries most of the flow while the artery carries most of the oxygen. (Book p983)

items.q: Assess the two supply statements: I The portal vein contributes the larger share of blood flow but the smaller share of oxygen. II The hepatic artery is annotated as contributing 60% of the blood supply.
items.exp: Portal vein 70% of blood but only 40% of oxygen, and hepatic artery 30% of blood with 60% of oxygen, so the second statement reverses the two percentages printed for the artery. (Book p983)

items.q: Fill up: The note under the portal tract diagram places the hepatic artery ______ to the portal vein and ______ to the bile duct.
items.exp: The short caption beside the triad sketch reads anterior to vein, left of bile duct, the classical arrangement in which the artery sits anteromedially while the portal vein lies posterior. (Book p983)

items.q: Assess the two capsule statements: I The central hepatic vein is described as the only structure not covered by Glisson's capsule. II The portal tract is drawn in the centre of the lobule and the hepatic vein at its periphery.
items.exp: The parenthetical note on the hepatic vein line states it is the only structure not covered by Glisson's capsule, and the figure puts the portal tracts at the periphery with the vein in between, the reverse of the second statement. (Book p983)

items.q: Which components does the diagram place in between the peripheral portal tracts and the central vein?
items.exp: The three levels of the structure list are periphery with the portal tract, in between with hepatocytes plus sinusoids, and centre with the hepatic vein, the two being connected by sinusoids. (Book p983)

items.q: The portal tract bracket in the diagram lists all of the following EXCEPT:
items.exp: The portal tract entry carries exactly three named structures, portal vein 70 over 40, hepatic artery 30 over 60 and bile duct, while the terminal hepatic vein belongs to the centre of the lobule. (Book p983)

items.q: Fill up: In the pathology line, liver lobules are ______ by nodules which are ______ by fibrous septae, and this ends as cirrhosis.
items.exp: The chain is written as liver lobules replaced by nodules, then connected by fibrous septae, then cirrhosis, which is the page's one-line definition of the architectural change. (Book p983)

items.q: Assess the two vessel-origin statements: I Sinusoids are traced to the vitelline vein, which the table shows taking over from the umbilical vein. II The common hepatic vein is listed as a derivative of the endodermal bud.
items.exp: The last row reads vitelline vein greater than umbilical vein giving sinusoids, and no hepatic vein appears in the derivatives table, whose rows end with the sinusoids. (Book p983)

items.q: A trainee labels a lobule diagram and is asked which element escapes the fibrous capsule that invests everything else at the periphery. Which structure should she name?
items.exp: Glisson's capsule accompanies the portal tract at the periphery, and the page singles out the hepatic vein at the centre as the only structure not covered by it. (Book p983)

items.q: Match each printed fraction with its figure — 1) 70 2) 60 3) 40 … A) Oxygen share from the hepatic artery B) Blood share from the portal vein C) Oxygen share from the portal vein
items.exp: The portal vein line carries 70 over 40, so 70 is its share of blood and 40 its share of oxygen, while 60 is the oxygen figure printed under the hepatic artery line. (Book p983)

items.q: Which single word links the peripheral portal tracts to the central vein in the diagram's blood flow arrow?
items.exp: The bracket running from the portal tract list to the hepatic vein is labelled connected by sinusoids, the in-between hepatocyte plates being perfused through them. (Book p983)
